evidence_frontier: The latest completed evidence includes the successful 100‑epoch w8 confirmation (seeds 42‑46) where alpha5_w8 achieved 444/500 correct versus control 448/500, meeting the gate alpha5_w8.aggregate_qant_correct >= alpha5_w16_control.aggregate_qant_correct - 10. Earlier experiments (Exp021) evaluated w8 and w12 with 10 seeds at 100 epochs, yielding aggregate correct 887 and 884 respectively, but the preregistered gate was not applied. No confirmation experiment for w12 has been completed. Alpha5 has been promoted based on readout redundancy improvements, and the next open question is whether a narrower local representation (width 12) can preserve performance under a fresh seed set.
analysis: Observation: Reducing local width to 8 can meet the performance gate when evaluated with a fresh seed set (42‑46). Observation: Width 12 has not yet been tested under the gate; prior aggregate correct (884) was lower than control (897) but without a gate assessment. Observation: The promotion of Alpha5 relied on readout redundancy, not on local width. Hypothesis: A local width of 12 will retain sufficient Q.ANT accuracy to satisfy the gate alpha5_w12.aggregate_qant_correct >= alpha5_w16_control.aggregate_qant_correct - 10 when evaluated with a new seed set at 100 epochs.
hypothesis: When evaluated on ECG200 with a fresh set of five seeds and 100 training epochs, the Alpha5 architecture using a local representation width of 12 (alpha5_w12) will achieve an aggregate Q.ANT correct count no more than 10 fewer than the 16‑width control (alpha5_w16_control), thereby passing the preregistered gate.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch w12 Confirmation on ECG200 with Fresh Seeds
proposal.research_question: Does reducing Alpha5's local representation width from 16 to 12 preserve performance and meet the preregistered gate on ECG200 when evaluated with a fresh seed set?
proposal.rationale: Prior evidence shows that a width‑8 local representation can meet the gate, while width‑12 has only been evaluated without gate verification. Confirming width‑12 will identify the minimal local width that maintains the promoted readout robustness, reducing model size without sacrificing Q.ANT accuracy.

procedure: Train each candidate for 100 epochs on the ECG200 training set using the same hyperparameters as previous Alpha5 experiments.
Evaluate Q.ANT predictions on the ECG200 test set for each seed.
Compute aggregate Q.ANT correct counts (5 seeds × 100 test samples = 500 predictions per candidate).
Apply the preregistered gate: candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10.

proposal.success_criteria: Alpha5_w12 must achieve aggregate_qant_correct >= alpha5_w16_control.aggregate_qant_correct - 10 on the 5‑seed, 500‑prediction evaluation (e.g., if control = 448, w12 must be ≥ 438).
proposal.risks: The w12 candidate may fail the gate, yielding no promotion and consuming compute budget. Using only five seeds limits statistical power; results could be seed‑specific. The experiment assumes the same training hyperparameters remain optimal for the narrower width, which may not hold.
